item.description: Wednesday evening bonus edition — three items on what AI-designed antibodies do in humans, why bigger protein language models are not always better for fitness prediction, and what AlphaFold 3 actually contributes to T-cell specificity prediction. First, Borriello/Koh/Troconiz/Nassirpour/Goyal et al. (Generate Biomedicines, J Infect Dis DOI 10.1093/infdis/jiag349, published 2026-07-14): first-in-human trial of GB-0669, a half-life-extended monoclonal antibody optimized using Generate's AI design platform and targeting the conserved S2 stem helix of the SARS-CoV-2 spike (an epitope with less selection pressure than the RBD). Preclinical safety in cynomolgus monkeys, then Phase 1 in 51 healthy adults 18-55 across five ascending single-IV cohorts (100, 300, 600, 1200, 2400 mg) with 43-week follow-up. All AEs mild (grade 1 or 2), no dose-limiting toxicities. Dose-proportional PK up to 2400 mg, terminal half-life 54 days (consistent with proper Fc engineering, comparable to nirsevimab). Dose-dependent serum live-virus neutralization at 600 and 1200 mg with separation from placebo; author-defined neutralizing index (serum concentration × in vitro potency) supports therapeutic coverage for ~2 weeks post-single-dose. In vitro combination testing with remdesivir/nirmatrelvir/molnupiravir shows improved neutralization profile. Proposed Phase 2 at 1200 mg for immunocompromised COVID-19 patients. Framing: this is the first-in-class fully-computationally-optimized commercial antibody to reach human safety readout, and it does not exhibit the hidden polyreactivity or PK weirdness that would falsify the AI-antibody design premise. Second, Hou/Liu/Zafar/Shen (Yufeng Shen lab, Columbia University, Nat Comput Sci DOI 10.1038/s43588-026-01010-z, published 2026-07-13; preprint 10.1101/2025.04.25.650688 v4): protein language models estimate p(sequence), which reflects the fitness landscape and is used for zero-shot mutation effect prediction. Widely believed in DL: bigger = better. This paper shows for fitness prediction it isn't. Across 154 ProteinGym experiments, models tested include ESM2 (all sizes), MSA-Transformer, EVE, ESM-IF1, ESM3. Performance is best in a moderate p(wildtype) regime; at very high p(wildtype) models predict uniformly high likelihoods for essentially all substitutions (nothing looks implausible relative to a well-memorized reference), and at very low p(wildtype) predict uniformly low likelihoods — both extremes collapse into uninformative noise. Larger models tend to push p(wildtype) higher, so scaling up moves many proteins above the moderate-p sweet spot and degrades fitness prediction, even though the larger model is objectively a better generative prior over natural sequences. Practical guideline: pick the model whose p(wildtype) sits in the moderate range for the target sequence, not the largest available model. Antibody-engineer implication: mid-sized antibody LMs (AntiBERTa/AbLang/IgLM in the ~100M-few×100M range) may already be in the right regime for CDR-scoring tasks; naive scaling to billions of parameters could be counterproductive. Third, McMaster/Elmoselhy/Ilievski/Thorpe/La Gruta/Rossjohn/Deane/Koohy (Hashem Koohy lab, University of Oxford, with Charlotte Deane and Jamie Rossjohn, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737208 v3, posted 2026-07-15): characterising AlphaFold 3's ability to predict T-cell antigen specificity. Built pipeline running AF3 for TCR:pMHC structure prediction >100× faster than default. Benchmarked AF3 and related structure-prediction models on IMMREP25 task. Underlying correlate of AF3-derived binding scores: dominant signal is positioning of the TCR over the pMHC (docking-pose plausibility), not the chemical detail of the interaction interface. Trained a small ML model (PAE Aggregator) on AF3's predicted aligned error output to produce a more calibrated binding score. With the refinement layer: (a) clusters sequence-similar TCRs by binding mode — geometric consistency a sequence-only model cannot see; (b) recapitulates mutational scanning experiments, correctly ranking point mutation effects. Take: AF3 is not a TCR specificity oracle — predictive signal comes disproportionately from pose plausibility rather than interface chemistry — but with task-appropriate scoring head it captures partial but real geometric regularities of TCR recognition. Direct parallel for antibody engineers: same architectural machinery used for antibody:antigen complexes; treat AF3 confidence scores as pose-plausibility, not affinity, and expect the practical utility to come from combining AF3 outputs with a task-appropriate scoring head.

item.title: Afternoon: Bloom lab real-time human neutralizing-antibody landscape to H3N2 subclade K and H1N1 D.3.1.1 — 27,409 titers across 91 HAs × 302 sera, subclade K strains with region D/E mutations further depress titers, informs 2026-2027 Northern Hemisphere vaccine strain selection (Fred Hutch, bioRxiv v2); Complete pseudovirus deep mutational scanning of RSV F for nirsevimab, clesrovimab, suptavumab, RSM01, 1A2, 1B6 in IgG and Fab form + biophysical model of how bivalent IgG buffers Fab-affinity-losing mutations, explaining why nirsevimab escape is subtype-B-biased (Fred Hutch/Bloom lab, bioRxiv v2); ProBuilder physics-based generative de novo design of protein binders for very small polar ligands including serotonin, dopamine, and zinc — crystal structures within <1 Å Cα RMSD of design, functional split-cpsfGFP dopamine and serotonin biosensors and split-NanoLuc zinc sensor (Longxing Cao lab, Westlake University, bioRxiv); ESM3 topology-guided decoding generates knotted proteins at 89% success rate vs ~0.5% for unguided diffusion, and shows knot topology is encoded distributively — 84% of sequence must be altered before knot breaks, with structural drift preceding topological disruption (Marsalkova/Simecek, CEITEC/Masaryk, bioRxiv v2)
item.description: Wednesday afternoon bonus edition — four items, thread is antibody escape and de novo binder generalization. First, Kikawa/Bloom et al. (Fred Hutch Cancer Center, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.02.18.706711 v2, posted 2026-07-14): "Near real-time data on the human neutralizing antibody landscape to influenza virus as of early 2026 to inform vaccine-strain selection." Barcoded pseudovirus sequencing-based neutralization assay: library of 53 recently circulating H3N2 + 30 recently circulating H1N1 hemagglutinins + 8 past vaccine strains = 91 HAs × 186 barcoded variants; panel of 302 human sera (ages 0-103, five geographic sites, mostly Oct-Nov 2025); 27,409 titers total. H3N2: median titers vary >3-fold across strains; subclade K (derived from J.2.4 with HA1 mutations K2N/S144N/N158D/I160K/Q173R/T328A) has significantly lower titers than all other current subclades; subvariants adding mutations in antigenic regions D (sites 96, 207, 223) and E (site 261) drop titers further. H1N1: subclade D.3.1.1 (from D.3.1 with R113K/A139D/E283K/K302E) has lower titers than parent D.3.1 and current NH vaccine strain. Age-stratified pattern in H1N1: adolescents and young adults have much lower titers to H1N1 strains with mutations at sites 155 or 157. Post-vaccination titer increases modest (~1.5-2.5× for H3N2, smaller for K and other newest subclades; regionD-mutated K variants get only ~1.5×) — data publicly available with Nextstrain integration for real-time vaccine-strain informed decisions. Second, Simonich/McMahon/Juviler/Bloom et al. (Fred Hutch, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.02.12.705519 v2, posted 2026-07-14): "Complete definition of how antibodies used to prevent RSV are affected by F mutations." v2 adds DMS for candidate antibodies 1A2 and 1B6, DMS against five human polyclonal sera, and expanded validation neutralization assays. Two pieces: (1) biophysical model — when Fab affinity is high, bivalent IgG binding buffers mutations that reduce Fab affinity; when Fab affinity is moderate, buffering vanishes. Nirsevimab has higher Fab affinity for RSV-A than RSV-B → escape mutations that look silent against RSV-A show measurable IgG neutralization loss against RSV-B. Validated with K68Q and (K/N)201S mutations. Implication: measure escape in Fab form for cross-strain generalizability. (2) Pseudovirus deep mutational scanning of near-all F-ectodomain point mutations in the subtype-A Long strain, measuring cell-entry fitness + neutralization by nirsevimab, clesrovimab, suptavumab, RSM01, 1A2, 1B6 (IgG + Fab) + 5 polyclonal human sera. New clesrovimab-escape sites identified: 426, 429, 433, 470 (beyond known 443, 445, 446). New nirsevimab escape substitutions beyond known 64-73/201-216 landscape. Escape scores validated against natural high-escape-score RSV strains; sporadic natural resistance seen but no sustained spread. Polyclonal sera: no single mutation reduces serum neutralization by more than a few-fold; mutations that do modestly affect sera cluster at F apex near nirsevimab epitope. Nextstrain-integrated escape trees for surveillance. Third, Zhang/Ke/Zhi/Jin/Cao et al. (Longxing Cao lab, Westlake University, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.13.738243, posted 2026-07-14): physics-based generative de novo design of small-molecule and metal-ion binders using ProBuilder — Rotamer Interaction Field (RIF) enumerates energetically favorable side-chain-ligand contacts, backbone construction anchored at RIF residues via Monte Carlo fragment assembly with joint RPX folding score + RIF binding score, sequences designed with Rosetta + ProteinMPNN + AlphaFold2 self-consistency filtering. Small-molecule results (helical bundles, mostly 120 aa, 5-6 helices): dolutegravir 14/96 designs bound, best 4.94 μM → 971 nM after helix-extension optimization; cianidanol 20/94; DFHBI 2/16; serotonin 6/38, best 72.8 μM → 29.9 μM after four rounds of sequence optimization; dopamine 1/33 at 75.0 μM (single binder — hardest target). Interface-disrupting mutations abolish binding, confirming designed pockets. Metals: 65-aa four-helix bundles designed to be metastable in absence of metal, folded on binding. Zinc binder ZK2: 150 nM KD, tetrahedral coordination, 1:1 stoichiometry, no binding to Cu²⁺/Co²⁺/Ni²⁺ (overrides Irving-Williams series). Nickel binder NiM4: 5.38 μM, octahedral, high selectivity. Crystal structures: serotonin-bound SRO_30 (2.58 Å, Cα RMSD 0.97 Å to design), dopamine-bound DPA_9 (2.47 Å, Cα RMSD 0.79 Å), zinc-bound ZK2 (1.23 Å, Cα RMSD 0.45 Å). Biosensor engineering: split-cpsfGFP serotonin sensor wcSRO30_1.0 with ΔF/F₀ 339.9%, EC50 539.9 μM, size 129 aa vs iSeroSnFR 272 aa; split-cpsfGFP dopamine sensor at ΔF/F₀ 37.5% (first reported soluble de novo dopamine biosensor); split-NanoLuc zinc sensor with EC50 ~73 nM and strong Zn selectivity. Fourth, Marsalkova/Simecek (CEITEC/Masaryk University, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.05.07.723606 v2, posted 2026-07-14): "Advancing Knotted Protein Design with ESM3: Guided Generation and Topological Insights." ESM3-SM (1.4B params, fp16 on A10G) with derivative-free guided decoding + Topoly Alexander-polynomial knot scoring achieves 89% (95% CI 81-94%) knotted-topology success from fully masked sequences, vs ~0.5% for unguided diffusion. Trefoil (3₁) most common in generated set (33/70 resolved); complex topologies up to 9 crossings produced. Generated knots have lower ESM3 pLDDT (0.32) / pTM (0.21) than real knots evaluated in the same pipeline (0.90 / 0.84) — treat as topology-enriched samples pending independent validation. Robustness on real knotted proteins: 84% sequence must be altered before knot breaks, sharp threshold not gradual; at 50% masking RMSD already 3.24 Å but knot probability 0.85; topology encoded distributively across sequence, decoupled from specific 3D arrangement. MLP on frozen mean-pooled ESM3 embeddings hits 97.1% knot classification accuracy. Generated proteins <15% sequence identity to any known knot (mean 11.6%, indistinguishable from random baseline), arguing against memorization. Transferable lesson for antibody-LM practitioners: guided decoding with a task-specific scorer as a lightweight steering primitive without fine-tuning, and evidence that general protein-LM embeddings encode distributed global features robustly enough for probing.

item.title: H3BERTa — CDR-H3-only 86M-parameter RoBERTa antibody language model matches AntiBERTa2 on repertoire embedding and hits 93% test accuracy on HIV bnAb classification (ETH Zurich, Patterns); Frozen AINN-P1 protein foundation-model embeddings beat from-scratch antibody-antigen ΔΔG ranker with linear probe alone, Spearman 0.42→0.53 (Ainnocence, bioRxiv); ML-driven closed-loop DBTL pipeline for multi-objective antibody formulation optimization across melting temperature, diffusivity, and high-concentration viscosity using GRAS excipients (Adv Sci); COMPASS + MATCH — modular split-antibody T-cell-engager platform with computational framework for patient-specific multi-specific dose composition, validated on CLL PBMC and human lymphoma xenograft (U Utah, Commun Biol); De novo oligomer-selective alpha-synuclein binders via deep-learning-based design + one round of partial diffusion, 1.94 nM KD, substoichiometric fibril inhibition (Sahtoe/Knowles labs, bioRxiv)
item.description: Wednesday morning briefing — five items, thematically about pushing more of the antibody-engineering pipeline into learned representations or automated closed loops. First, Salaris/Pinter/Cioppi et al. (ETH Zurich, Patterns DOI 10.1016/j.patter.2026.101561, published 2026-07-10): H3BERTa — a RoBERTa-architecture transformer with ~86M parameters trained on ~18M CDR-H3 sequences from the Observed Antibody Space (OAS) database (IgG + IgA from healthy unvaccinated donors), MLM objective, 113 epochs, final loss 1.58. Head-to-head with AntiBERTa2 (pretrained on full heavy variable regions). UMAP: H3BERTa clusters primarily by J-gene (IGHJ segments contribute CDR-H3 C-terminus), AntiBERTa2 primarily by V-gene (accesses framework). Both models yield strongly bimodal LDA separation of naive vs memory B cells and support antigen-binding discrimination on immunized alpaca sequences (SARS-CoV-2 spike, human IL-6, human TNF-α) with comparable separability. HIV-1 bnAb classifier: linear-kernel SVM on frozen H3BERTa embeddings against a 390-CDR-H3 labeled set (bnAbs from CATNAP + hard negatives from OAS) achieves 93% test accuracy, macro-F1 0.92; GAN-H3BERTa semi-supervised variant yields more structured latent space with similar classification. Applied blind to a full HIV-1 donor bcr repertoire, both classifiers correctly place the experimentally validated bnAb and two other neutralizers in high-confidence bnAb regions. Repertoire-level PPL analysis on ~4.4M healthy + ~4.2M bnAb-donor sequences (Roskin et al.): central PPL distribution overlaps, but tails differ statistically — healthy repertoires higher PPL in upper tail, opposite direction in lower tail; low-PPL sequences enriched in tyrosine and longer loops (consistent with affinity-matured contacts), high-PPL sequences shorter and leucine-rich. Practical take: scope of input matters as much as parameter count for repertoire tasks; H3BERTa is species-agnostic (CDR-H3 is least species-specific) and enables full-repertoire-scale mining at fraction of the compute of full-variable-region models. Second, Wang/Jin/Pan (Ainnocence, Inc., bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.13.738250, posted 2026-07-14; competing interest — commercial model): frozen protein foundation-model embeddings for antibody-antigen ΔΔG ranking. Affinity maturation cast as learning-to-rank over point mutations. Under identical 5-fold CV, a regularized linear probe on frozen AINN-P1 (autoregressive protein foundation model) embeddings already exceeds a from-scratch task-specific end-to-end baseline; an optimized lightweight head raises mean Spearman rank correlation from 0.42 to 0.53 (~28% relative), trains in seconds without any foundation-model fine-tuning. Interpretation: linear probe beating end-to-end model implies the gain is representation quality, not downstream capacity. Frozen Spearman 0.53 is moderate, not strong — framed as lower bound expected to be exceeded by task-adaptive fine-tuning. Third, "Automation and Active Learning for the Multi-Objective Optimization of Antibody Formulations" (Advanced Science DOI 10.1002/advs.76551, published 2026-07-13): closed-loop DBTL pipeline for GRAS-restricted excipient formulation. ML predictor of formulation behavior trained on multi-objective outputs (melting temperature as stability proxy, translational diffusivity, high-concentration viscosity). Automation-assisted formulation produces dozens of unique compositions on demand; results feed back into next round of model-designed experiments. Pipeline converges on both improved formulations and accurate predictive models across objectives; models map underlying property-function landscape (not just point-optimize). Operationalizes developability as an active-learning problem. Fourth, Kendell/McShinsky/Modzelewska et al./Gambles (U Utah, Commun Biol DOI 10.1038/s42003-026-10602-4, published 2026-07-13; MATCH IP pending): MATCH — modular split-antibody T-cell engager platform assembling multi-specific engagers over CD19/CD20/CD38 for B-cell malignancies. COMPASS — computational framework integrating T-cell counts, tumor burden, antigen expression to predict individualized multi-specific therapy compositions maximizing tumor kill while preserving T-cell viability (T-cell exhaustion treated as hard cost). Validation: (1) COMPASS predictions match effective formulations on CLL patient PBMC; (2) COMPASS-predicted compositions produced significantly improved survival in human lymphoma xenograft mouse model. Lab-in-the-loop: patient measurement → prediction → per-patient composition. Antibody-engineer implication: bispecific/multispecific design value shifts from finding the single best construct to producing composable specificities the framework can mix at point of care. Fifth, Zhang/Han/Ortigosa-Pascual et al. (Sahtoe + Knowles groups, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.13.738012, posted 2026-07-14): potent substoichiometric inhibition of alpha-synuclein aggregation by de novo oligomer-binding proteins. Target: intrinsically disordered NAC domain of α-synuclein, which lacks stable epitope but preferentially adopts extended β-strand upon assembly engagement — binders designed to present matching β-strand recognition scaffold and stabilise that conformer. Deep-learning-based protein design → 21 expressed → 3 engage target in vitro and in live cells. One round of partial diffusion (partial noise + re-denoise conditioning on target) as affinity-maturation step; best binder KD 1.94 nM, no detectable cross-reactivity to tau/amylin/amyloid-β. Solution NMR confirms peptide association and conformational changes consistent with intended architecture. Kinetic modeling with seeded-aggregation experiments + monomer/oligomer/fibril affinities resolves the specific microscopic step each binder inhibits: most potent binder selectively captures on-pathway oligomers (species most tied to neurotoxicity) and suppresses fibril formation at substoichiometric ratios without engaging bulk monomer pool. Transferable lesson: partial diffusion works as an affinity-maturation operator — no full redesign cycle needed to go from functional-but-modest to nanomolar, parallels the RFantibody-family workflow for antibody CDR maturation.

item.title: Night: ESM3 geometric atlas — modality fusion between layers 25–35 with sequence joining last after layer 28; functional annotation permanently orthogonal; structural disorder delays fusion (Steenwyk, bioRxiv); Schneidman-Duhovny lab review of deep learning for adaptive immune receptor structure prediction and design — AIR-specific LMs, inverse folding, diffusion backbone generation, sequence-space diffusion, challenges in CDR-loop modeling and epitope-specific design (Hebrew University, Curr Opin Struct Biol)
item.description: Night edition — two items. First, Steenwyk (Life Sciences Research Foundation / Vanderbilt, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737319, posted 2026-07-12): "A geometric atlas of how ESM3 organizes modalities across depth." Representational-similarity analysis applied to ESM3-sm-open-v1 (1.4B parameters, 48 transformer layers) once per modality in isolation across all 48 layers; 5,555 proteins from 12 organisms spanning bacteria, archaea, and eukaryotes. The five input modalities are: amino-acid sequence, 3D structure, SS8 (8-state secondary structure), SASA (solvent accessibility), and functional annotations. Key findings: (1) Four physical modalities (sequence, structure, SS8, SASA) begin in distinct subspaces, remain maximally separated through ~layer 25, then fuse into a shared low-dimensional subspace between layers 25–35. Fusion is ordered — structure-derived modalities (structure, SS8, SASA) are mutually aligned from the input and fuse with each other first; sequence joins last, after layer 28. (2) Functional annotation never fuses: remains representationally orthogonal to physical modalities at every layer, whether annotation is whole-protein or per-residue — content-driven, not tokenization artifact. (3) Fusion is a learned property: absent in a randomly-initialized model of the same architecture. (4) Fusion reorganizes variance: between-condition variance converts to within-condition variance while the stream never approaches isotropy. (5) Fusion depth is independent of protein length but delayed by structural disorder. (6) Universal: all 12 organisms across all superkingdoms peak at the same network depth (layer 35). Practical implications: adapter insertion before layer 28 preserves the pre-fusion sequence representation; the 25–35 band is richest for structural probing; functional-annotation orthogonality means annotation tokens do not corrupt physical-property representations; disordered regions (including CDR loops) fuse modalities later than framework residues, a mechanistic account of why CDR modeling is harder. Second, Cohen/Hochner/Schneidman-Duhovny (Hebrew University, Curr Opin Struct Biol DOI 10.1016/j.sbi.2026.103326, published 2026-07-10): review of deep-learning progress for adaptive immune receptors (antibodies + TCRs). Covers AIR-specific language models, structure prediction, epitope-conditioned design. Generative strategies reviewed: inverse folding, diffusion-based backbone generation, sequence-space diffusion, sequence-structure co-design. Datasets and evaluation metrics discussed with explicit sources of bias and need for improved benchmarks. Challenges enumerated: flexible CDR-loop modeling, reliable AIR-antigen complex ranking, scalable epitope-specific AIR design. Full text paywalled; abstract-only summary here.

item.title: Evening: GB-0669 — first-in-human Phase 1 of an AI-designed monoclonal antibody targeting SARS-CoV-2 spike S2 stem helix (Generate Biomedicines, J Infect Dis) — n=51, 100–2400 mg IV ascending doses, 54-day half-life, dose-dependent serum live-virus neutralization at 600/1200 mg with 2-week neutralizing-index window, no DLTs; Nat Comput Sci mechanistic account of why bigger protein language models degrade at fitness prediction — model performance depends on how well p(sequence) matches evolutionary patterns, with a moderate-likelihood sweet spot; larger models push wildtype p(sequence) past the sweet spot into a compressed high-end where mutation rankings degenerate (Shen lab, Columbia); PeptideCLM-2 — SMILES-based chemical language model suite trained on >100M molecules for therapeutic-peptide native representation, beats prior methods on membrane diffusion, biological function, and half-life prediction (Novo Nordisk Molecular AI + UT Austin, J Chem Inf Model); MDMI — two-stage structure-guided peptide-design pipeline from tiny labeled datasets, structure-aware predictor + genetic algorithm cuts an all-negative false-positive rate from 70% to near zero and yields 4× more in-silico binders than baselines; split-GFP wet-lab testbed hits 38% sequence divergence with function retained in stage 1 and >50% in stage 2 (Pardee lab, U Toronto, bioRxiv)
item.description: Tuesday evening supplement — four items. First, Borriello/Koh/Snyder/De Alwis (Generate Biomedicines, J Infect Dis DOI 10.1093/infdis/jiag349, published 2026-07-14): first published Phase-1 trial of an AI-designed monoclonal antibody. GB-0669 targets the conserved SARS-CoV-2 spike S2 stem helix (not the variable RBD), a region under limited immune selective pressure and thus a candidate for variant-resilient neutralization. Half-life-extended Fc. Randomized double-blind placebo-controlled first-in-human: n=51 healthy adults 18–55, five ascending IV doses (100/300/600/1200/2400 mg), 36 GB-0669 / 15 placebo, 43-week follow-up. Pre-clinical safety in cynomolgus monkeys clean. No DLTs; all AEs grade 1 or 2. Dose-proportional PK to 2400 mg, half-life 54 days. Dose-dependent serum live-virus neutralization at 600 and 1200 mg with clear placebo separation; neutralizing index (concentration × in-vitro potency) supports therapeutic-level activity for ~2 weeks post-dose. Combination in-vitro with remdesivir, nirmatrelvir, molnupiravir shows improved neutralization profiles. Supports Phase-2 at 1200 mg in immunocompromised patients. Paper does not detail the internal AI design pipeline (proprietary Generate platform integrating sequence/structure/developability), but this is the first published clinical readout for an antibody carrying the AI-designed label — the "developability/in-vivo PK wall" prediction against generative antibody design is now falsified on at least one molecule. Phase-2 efficacy remains to be shown. Second, Hou/Liu/Zafar/Shen (Columbia University Irving Medical Center, Systems Biology + Biomedical Informatics + Sulzberger Genome Center + Program for Mathematical Genomics, Nat Comput Sci DOI 10.1038/s43588-026-01010-z, published 2026-07-13): "Understanding language model scaling for protein fitness prediction." Mechanistic account of the well-known but under-explained anomaly that protein-LM fitness-prediction performance peaks at intermediate model size and declines beyond it. Zero-shot mutation-effect prediction uses model-assigned p(sequence) as fitness proxy, with mutant/wildtype likelihood ratio for ranking. Authors show model size, training-set composition, and stochastic training bias predicted p(sequence) away from real fitness. Performance depends on how well p(sequence) matches evolutionary patterns in homologs — best achieved at a moderate p(sequence) level. At extreme predicted wildtype likelihoods, models emit uniformly low or high likelihoods for nearly all mutations and ranking degenerates. Larger models tend to assign higher p(sequence) to observed sequences (sharper natural-distribution modeling), pushing many proteins past the moderate sweet spot into the compressed high-end — the mechanism by which scale hurts fitness prediction. Practical implication: check wildtype p(sequence) under the model before assuming bigger is better; consider ensembling across sizes; motivates antibody-specific LMs whose training distribution places antibody wildtypes in the moderate-likelihood band. Companion "Perspective" piece by Wang (Tsinghua) frames the same argument. Third, Feller/Secor/Swanson/Wilke/Deibler (Novo Nordisk Molecular AI + UT Austin Integrative Biology, J Chem Inf Model DOI 10.1021/acs.jcim.6c00652, published 2026-07-13): PeptideCLM-2 — a suite of SMILES-based chemical language models trained on >100M molecules with curated peptide-scale sequences, targeting the modality gap between protein LMs (restricted to canonical amino acids) and small-molecule chemical LMs (choke on polymer-length peptides). Native representation of non-canonical amino acids, N-methylation, cyclization, D-amino acids, non-peptide moieties. Benchmarks on three therapeutic-peptide endpoints (membrane diffusion, biological function, half-life) beat prior methods including static chemical descriptors and custom multi-embedding pipelines. Antibody-relevance: technology-transfer path toward SMILES-scale models for ADCs (antibody-payload-linker triples) and low-data-regime developability prediction. Fourth, Bayat/Perkins/Pardee (University of Toronto, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.13.737974, posted 2026-07-14, body not yet rendered — abstract-only): MDMI — Minimal Data Maximal Insight — two-stage structure-guided pipeline for functional peptide variants from tiny (tens-to-hundreds) annotated datasets. Stage 1 uses ML predictor on 3D structural features from predicted peptide-protein complexes (interface geometry + binding energetics) paired with a genetic algorithm. Structure-aware featurization cuts false-positive rate from 70% (sequence-only baseline) to near zero on an all-negative benchmark and produces ~4× more high-confidence in-silico binders than SOTA peptide/protein-design baselines. Wet-lab testbed uses split-GFP fluorescence readout for peptide-protein complementation: Stage 1 hits up to 38% sequence divergence from wildtype with retained activity; Stage 2 motif-guided recombination of Stage 1 successes reaches >50% divergence and reveals two functional clusters in sequence space. Full-length GFP fusion of a top candidate retains GFP-like emission, supporting fluorescent-scaffold formation. Transferable pattern for antibody CDR redesign — small labeled datasets, need diverse alternatives retaining same-epitope binding — where "predicted peptide-protein complex" swaps to "predicted antibody-antigen complex" and split-GFP swaps to an affinity assay.

item.title: TEDlm — domain-centric protein language model beats ESM-2-3B on CATH S40 remote homology at 650M params (AUROC1 0.28 vs 0.22); TEDlm3D with distance-guided contact loss reaches 0.50, matching Foldseek from sequence alone (Jones lab, UCL, bioRxiv); de novo conformation-selective miniprotein modulators of focal adhesion kinase — 33/96 designs modulate activity, low-nM inhibitors and 2×+ activators, cross-kinase redesign to Src (Baker lab, bioRxiv); AlphaFold3 audit across 5 application areas — uneven performance, training-set-adjacency dependence, model confidence fails on protein-RNA (Beltrao lab, U Fribourg/Lausanne, bioRxiv); ESM3-SM guided decoding + Topoly Alexander-polynomial scoring hits 89% knotted-protein success vs 0.5% unguided diffusion, 84% sequence perturbation before knot breaks (bioRxiv); asymmetric structural transfer — language-to-biology transfer strengthens with scale (drop 0.08), biology-to-language decays toward chance (drop 0.36), replicated across ESM-2 and ProtBERT (bioRxiv)
item.description: Monday morning briefing — five items, all posted 2026-07-13 or 2026-07-14, strong methodological day. First, Wei/Kandathil/Buchan/Jones (UCL, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.09.737428, posted 2026-07-13): TEDlm — masked language model pre-trained on structurally-defined domain segments from The Encyclopedia of Domains rather than full-length UniRef sequences. Standard MLM objective; TEDlm3D variant adds a distance-guided contact loss supervising attention maps against Cα–Cα geometry during pre-training. On CATH S40 remote-homology (<40% identity), 650M TEDlm scores AUROC1 0.28 at final layer vs ESM-2 3B at 0.22 — domain-centric pretraining beats 5× parameter scale-up. TEDlm3D reaches 0.50, approaching Foldseek's structure-based 0.53 from sequence at inference. Contact signal is in the encoder itself: attention-map probes and categorical Jacobian recover contact structure, not just a trained head. Zero-shot Molecular Function prediction substantially better than ESM-2; biophysical property tasks (dominated by local composition) comparable. Direct implication for antibody-LM builders: antibody variable domains are exactly one TED domain, argues restricted-domain pretraining (AntiBERTy, AbLang, IgLM) was correct choice; TEDlm3D contact loss transfers cleanly to paired-structure pretraining with SAbDab/AF3-multimer/IgFold coordinates. Second, Bauer/Lee et al./Baker (UW IPD + collaborators, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.10.737808, posted 2026-07-13, body not yet rendered — abstract-only): de novo genetically encoded miniprotein binders targeting focal adhesion kinase (FAK) with conformation-selective framing — each design targeted to stabilize a specific FAK conformational state (active vs inactive). 96 designs → 33 modulate kinase activity (~34% hit rate consistent with modern RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN+AF filter pipelines). Top 4 characterized: 2 inhibitors with low-nM IC50s, 2 activators (>2× activity potentiation). Modulators preserve in-vitro directional effects in cells. Cross-kinase transfer: FAK inhibitors redesigned computationally to target Src kinase work — platform-level result. Design pipeline not spelled out in abstract but authorship + framing implies standard RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN + AF-filter stack; novelty is conformation-selective scaffolding and demonstration that both inhibition and activation are accessible from the same platform. Complements antibody engineering — intracellular targets are outside the antibody-accessible space. Third, Follonier/Liu et al./Beltrao (U Fribourg + U Lausanne, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.13.738147, posted 2026-07-13, body not yet rendered — abstract-only): audit of AlphaFold3 across five application areas — ubiquitinated protein structure, TCR–peptide-MHC recognition, antibody-antigen complexes, protein-RNA, protein-lipid. Headline: AF3's extension to new biomolecule types shows less consistent performance and generalisation than AF2's monomer/multimer gains. Accuracy in several tasks depends on presence of related complexes in the training set (memorization/adjacency effect). Specific critical finding: in protein-RNA predictions, model confidence fails to separate genuine from decoy interaction partners — confidence metric untrustworthy for RNA-target screening. Antibody-antigen task included; specific number pending body render but consistent with "good in favourable settings, dependent on training-set overlap, less broadly generalisable than AF2" — matches anecdotal experience with novel epitopes and unusual CDR H3 / germline usage. Practical frame: AF3 is powerful for hypothesis generation and prioritisation but confidence metrics must be used with awareness of training-set overlap on an application-by-application basis. Fourth, "Advancing Knotted Protein Design with ESM3" (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.05.07.723606, posted 2026-07-14): ESM3-SM (1.4B params, smallest open-source variant, fp16 on NVIDIA A10G via Modal) with derivative-free guided decoding using Topoly Alexander-polynomial scoring (30 random-projection stochastic closures per evaluation) to design knotted proteins. Guided ESM3 achieves 89% success (95% CI 81–94%) vs ~0.5% for unguided diffusion (RFdiffusion, EvoDiff) — dramatic gap but explicitly guided-vs-unguided not architecture-matched. Robustness: 84% of sequence must be perturbed on average before knot breaks; loss follows sharp threshold not gradual degradation; structural drift (RMSD) accumulates well before topology fails — topology more robust than specific 3D arrangement in ESM3 representation. Generated knot types include trefoil (33), figure-eight (10), torus 5₂ (10), plus 8₁₉, 9₄₄, 9₄₅. No close sequence similarity to known knotted proteins (KnotProt/AlphaKnot 2.0) — not memorization. Practical for structurally unusual antibody scaffolds — cyclic-permuted VHHs, disulphide-constrained topologies. Fifth, "Asymmetric Structural Transfer Between Natural Language and Biological Foundation Models" (bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.09.737502, posted 2026-07-13, abstract only): reverse-transfer study asking whether protein LMs fine-tuned on English structural tasks acquire zero-shot linguistic competence, in the same way English-fine-tuned LMs had been shown to acquire zero-shot protein-homology discrimination. Answer: reverse transfer is consistently weak, does not exceed matched-token controls, does not scale, does not generalize. Architecture-matched 2×2 with known training data (eliminates pretraining-contamination confound): language→biology off-domain drop 0.08 vs biology→language 0.36. Scaling widens the gap — language-to-biology strengthens with size, biology-to-language decays toward chance. Replicated across ESM-2 and ProtBERT families. Implication: initializing specialized biological models from general-purpose LMs is asymmetrically favoured over the reverse; "biological sequences are just another language" fails in operationally symmetric sense.

item.title: Night: BCR-Mistral — 500M-parameter decoder-only DNA BCR language model beats ESM-2-650M and Ab-RoBERTa on MS-associated repertoire embedding across 11.5M IGH sequences (Krishnan/Macklin, U Colorado Anschutz, bioRxiv); RFdiffusion+ProteinMPNN motif-scaffolding of N-Myc TAD yields single-digit-nM Aurora-A miniprotein inhibitors with crystal-structure-verified αG-helix + activation-loop convergent signature (Bayliss lab, Leeds, bioRxiv); Blood Transcriptional Module aggregation beats gene-level features by 14–25 AUC points on pan-vaccine (influenza/HepB/YF) high-responder prediction across 1,032 participants (Tomic/Przytycki, Boston U, bioRxiv)
item.description: Monday night supplement — three items, all posted 2026-07-13. First, Peet/Krishnan/Macklin (University of Colorado Anschutz Medical Campus, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.07.735316): BCR-Mistral — nucleotide-level decoder-only DNA foundation model for BCR IGH sequences, downscaled from Mistral-7B architecture; three variants at 100M/300M/500M parameters, 500M model kept. Trained on ~2M heterogeneous OPIG OAS IGH sequences selected by iterative random sampling in 7-mer Euclidean space; nucleotide-level tokenization, random rotation, up to two 20-nt attention masks, up to one-third length truncation as augmentation; AdamW, effective batch 2400, 8 AMD MI100 GPUs. Outperforms ESM-2-650M and Ab-RoBERTa on same-disease-different-patient embedding triplet distances and cosine similarity; protein-tokenized variant of same architecture on same corpus performs worse than DNA variant, arguing nucleotide tokens capture codon-bias / silent-mutation signal beyond protein level. Downstream: 3-layer MLP classifier (256/128/64) on last-token embeddings for 5-way disease classification (healthy / autoimmune / infectious / other / MS); custom "dynamic exclusion" loss progressively drops MS sequences confidently classified as non-MS from the loss (analogous to semi-hard example mining), raising held-out precision. Study-grouped (not patient-grouped) CV folds surface study-driven artifacts. Data foundation: exhaustive NCBI SRA reanalysis of "multiple sclerosis" runs (December 2024 snapshot) with manual metadata curation + TRUST4 assembly + OPIG OAS = 11.5M IGH sequences from ~800 patients, 2.8M with full VDJ. Patient-level: 128-waypoint fixed-D repertoire embedding via joint reconstruction+contrastive optimization in hidden-state space; XGBoost on waypoint + sequence-classification inputs; ROC AUC >0.8 for MS vs healthy/infectious, lower for MS vs other autoimmune. Validation: correctly ranks 3/4 known PLP1c-binding myelin-specific IgGs above isotype control; longitudinal fingolimod/natalizumab treatment reduces disease-associated repertoire fraction (n small, not individually significant but direction consistent). Confirmed antibody binding to O4+ oligodendrocytes by flow. Code (upon publication) at github.com/krishnanlab/bcr-mistral-final; weights + processed data at Zenodo 20432913. Second, Miles/Bayliss (University of Leeds + University of Oxford Gergely lab, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.12.737516): RFdiffusion motif-scaffolding of N-Myc TAD residues 73–84 (short) and 73–89 (long) with Aurora-A hotspots, ~3,893 backbones across two motif sets, ProteinMPNN 1–2 seqs/backbone, AF2-initial-guess filter (iPAE<10, pLDDT>84, 2.5–3% hit rate); 17 designs selected. 15 express in E. coli, 8 inhibit Aurora-A ADP-Glo with fittable IC50s. Top designs DBS1 (IC50 12 nM, KD 0.9 nM by ITC — sub-nanomolar), DBS5 (IC50 16 nM), DBL5 (IC50 31 nM, KD 3 nM). ~1000× affinity gain over parent N-Myc peptide (KD ~12 μM). 9 crystal structures at 1.79–2.9 Å reveal convergent design signature — extensive αG-helix engagement via C-terminal helix + hydrogen bond / main-chain contact to activation loop; weak binders have shorter/bent C-terminal helices. DBL5 H55A mutation removes activation-loop H-bond → 10× IC50 loss to 425 nM, causally confirms the pattern. Aurora-B selectivity: DBS1 retains weak Aurora-B activity (100× less than Aurora-A), other selective binders essentially inactive on Aurora-B in ADP-Glo. Kinase-structure basis for selectivity: M233→L289 in P+1 pocket + non-conserved αG-helix residues Y334/Q335 in Aurora-A vs Aurora-B/C. Cellular: HeLa GFP-fusion transfections reduce Aurora-A T288 autophosphorylation at spindle poles for DBL5 and DBS1; DBS1 (only) also modestly reduces Histone H3 pS10; IP-MS: DBL5/DBS2/DBS5 pull down only Aurora-A + TPX2 as common interactors (24–42 proteins each), DBS1 promiscuous (215 interactors including MARK2, MELK). AF3 ternary Aurora-A/DBS1/TPX2 model supports simultaneous binding (ipTM 0.81/0.96). Design-to-hit ratio unusually good (17 designs, 13 with measurable inhibition, sub-nM hit) argues motif-scaffolding from natural weak binder is lower-variance than de novo. Third, Hao/Tomic/Przytycki (Boston University Bioinformatics + NEIDL + Chobanian & Avedisian SOM, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737303): interpretable ML for shared and vaccine-specific immune architectures. Harmonized ISDR/HIPC dataset, 1,032 participants with matched pre/post-vax transcriptomics + ~day-28 antibody titers across influenza (n=776), HepB (n=160), and yellow fever (n=96). Independent random-forest classifiers per pathogen. Blood Transcriptional Module aggregation dominates raw gene-level features: AUC lifts 0.56→0.78 (HepB), 0.54→0.70 (influenza), 0.56→0.81 (YF). Permutation feature-importance: HepB driven by Th2 differentiation, integrin leukocyte migration, pDCs, M1 macrophages, B-cell modules; influenza by CD4+ T, M2 macrophage, c-MYC + mitotic cell cycle; yellow fever by BCR signaling, B-cell development, CORO1A-DEF6, MAIT, NK. Surrogate decision trees extract if-then rules with numerical thresholds. Cross-pathogen concordance identifies 4 shared transcriptional modules. Age but not sex residualization applied. Predicts peak (day-28) titer despite paper's framing; four shared modules are consistently-predictive-across-independent-models rather than jointly-modeled. Operational take for antibody engineers: BTM signatures identified are candidate stratification biomarkers for enriching high-responder repertoires in downstream discovery.

item.description: Afternoon supplement — three antibody/protein-design items today. First, Tennenhouse/Fleishman (Weizmann Institute of Science, bioRxiv 10.64898/2025.12.10.693474 v2, posted 2026-07-13): CADAbRe — end-to-end computational design of an entire synthetic antibody repertoire with drug-like properties. Pipeline: (1) combine all human V+J germline segments, graft 141 experimentally-determined CDR H3s, generate ~150k combinations; (2) atomistic modeling with CUMAb + independent A-Body-Builder-2 fold check, flag disagreements as prone to misfolding; (3) EpiNNet ML strategy selects freely-combinable germline+H3 sets from Rosetta energy + foldability labels — 10 sets containing 35k sequences, 85% predicted stable, >700 unique light-heavy V-gene pairs (2 orders of magnitude more than recent synthetic repertoires); (4) Rosetta atomistic H3 diversification with immutable stability-critical residues, developability filters (no Met/Cys/N-glycosylation). Largest set expanded to ~450 V-gene pairs, 240k designed H3s, assembled by one-pot Golden Gate + phage display of Fabs at <$10^-4 per variant, 10-day turnaround, 5×10^8 unique antibodies. Panning against HEWL, SARS-CoV-2 RBD, mouse FLT3, and Lujo virus spike: 13 designed binders from <150 sequenced colonies, 12/13 exactly match a designed sequence, spanning 5 heavy V genes, 6 light V genes, 6 parental H3 scaffolds; EC50 0.3–11 nM comparable to clinical benchmarks where available; 9 expressed cleanly as IgG1 with yields above historical average. Developability suite (nanoDSF, BVP/CIC, SEC/AC-SINS/DLS, HIC) benchmarked against 12 clinical-stage antibodies including Adalimumab and Pembrolizumab: all designs Tagg>74°C and Tm>69°C, most low nonspecific binding and low self-association; 3/9 flagged for hydrophobicity (2 of these against RBD, consistent with anti-RBD antibody class). Repertoire available for academic research. Second, An/Cho/Kim (Yonsei + Institut Pasteur Korea + POSTECH, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.10.737702, posted 2026-07-13): de novo mini-protein binder mini-19 targeting CD81 large extracellular loop to block HCV entry. RFdiffusion (60–80 aa, 3-helix bundle topology, hotspot at L162/V169/I182/F186, noise 0.5) → 5000 backbones → 44 pass pAE<5.99; ProteinMPNN 1000 sequences per scaffold → filter pAE<4.7; AlphaFold2 validation with critical methodological finding — truncated soluble CD81 template exposes hydrophobic surfaces naturally shielded by transmembrane region, driving off-target binding artifacts; single ipTM threshold insufficient, requires multi-model consensus (≥2 of 5 AF2 models agree on backbone conformation with ipTM>0.83 + pLDDT>85) to eliminate false positives. 20 leads → 15 express cleanly at tens of mg/L E. coli → 8 bind CD81-LEL by SPR at 1 μM. Lead mini-19: KD 0.5 nM (ka 7.4×10^5 M^-1 s^-1, kd 3.8×10^-4 s^-1), monodisperse monomer, α-helical CD signature retained to 95°C without cooperative unfolding, HCVcc IC50 1.2 nM, native cell-surface CD81 recognition confirmed by flow cytometry and super-resolution imaging; sibling mini-20 same scaffold 48× weaker at 24 nM. MD suggests structural clamp locking closed conformation. Transferable ipTM+backbone-convergence recipe for any design task on truncated soluble receptor construct. Third, Cao lab et al. (Adv Sci, DOI 10.1002/advs.76522; preprint bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.03.20.713312, published 2026-07-13): breadth-restoration by database-mined somatic hypermutation grafting. Germline IGHV3-53 antibody HB148 (0 SHMs) neutralizes SARS-CoV-2 wild-type/Alpha/Delta (NT50 1–2 μg/mL) but escapes at Omicron BA.1. 3.04-Å crystal structure of HB148/wild-type RBD shows class-1 epitope, heavy chain 69% BSA, contacts Y421/Y453/A475; Omicron K417N/S477N/Q493R/Y505H remodels epitope. Enrichment analysis in CoV-AbDab IGHV3-53 sequences with BA.1 neutralization data identifies four consensus SHMs (VH G26E and T28I in CDR H1; VH S53P and Y58F in CDR H2). HB148-M4 (all four): ~100× KD improvement to both WT and BA.1 RBD; individual G26E/S53P/Y58F each 8–10× — approximately additive, distinct paratope-epitope contacts. Neutralizes WT/BA.1/BA.4-5 pseudoviruses (NT50 0.19–1.56 μg/mL); still no XBB.1.5 rescue at 100 μg/mL. Grafted onto four other IGHV3-53 antibodies (C1A-F10, P5A-3C8, BG4-25, LY-CoV488), M4 restores BA.1 binding for 3 of 4 (C1A-F10 exception gains WT affinity only). Structural mechanism: G26E extends contact to RBD residues 477–478, restoring interactions lost to S477N; S53P + Y58F improve interface packing. Ceiling of any single such patch is limited but a much more focused strategy than DMS for breadth-engineering. Limitations: surrogate/pseudovirus assays throughout; consensus-mining is retrospective not de novo prediction.

item.title: Inverse-design proteome mapping for Zα interactors via RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN (Poptsova lab, HSE Moscow) — YTHDC1 poly-E docks to ADAR1 Zα as a Z-RNA mimic; ProtBLIP2-SST — SaProt + Q-Former + Galactica multimodal (sequence, structure, text) protein-caption generator (Luo lab, HKUST)
item.description: Monday briefing. Two items — day is thin on antibody-specific work. First, Gromak, Shaytan, Herbert, and Poptsova (HSE University Moscow + InsideOutBio, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737312, posted 2026-07-12): "inverse computational design" pipeline that repurposes the de novo binder-design stack (RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN) as a proteome-search tool. 1,200 backbones across four batches (unconditional; hotspot-conditioned on K169/K170/N173/R174/Y177; C2'-atom-of-Z-RNA custom potential; hotspot+potential hybrid); 8 sequences per backbone via ProteinMPNN (~10,000 designs); ColabFold filter pLDDT>80, iPAE<10 Å, interface backbone RMSD<3 Å — 2 Å is too strict (5 hits), 3 Å relaxation gives 11 template binders; 11 templates queried against SWISS-PROT by BLASTp (e<1e-5) yielding ~1,200 regions across 298 proteins; four-metric co-folding filter (pDockQ, pDockQ2, ipTM, ipSAE) narrows to 79 candidates; full-length AlphaFold3 modeling with ADAR1p150. Key methodological finding — global scores (ipTM, ipSAE) fail on IDR-heavy complexes; interface-local pDockQ + ≥10 Cα-Cα contact pairs (<8 Å) required for discrimination. Top hit: YTHDC1 poly-E disordered region (residues 199–254) docks into Zα basic pocket via charge complementarity mimicking Z-RNA phosphate backbone (contacts K169, K170, R174). Confirmed by 1 μs Amber ff19SB MD: binary complex equilibrates by 200 ns, global RMSD ~8 Å, Zα–poly-E interface stays <3 Å throughout; ternary +dsRNA simulation shows all four interfaces <2.5 Å across dimeric assembly; deaminase does not adopt editing-competent geometry — catalytically dormant. No wet-lab validation yet (proposed: co-IP, SPR, K169A/K170A/R174A mutagenesis). Transferable pipeline for antibody paratope-mimic discovery. Second, Zhuoyang Chen and Qiong Luo (HKUST-Guangzhou / HKUST, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.10.737551, posted 2026-07-12): ProtBLIP2-SST — BLIP-2 framework rewired for proteins bridging sequence + structure + text for free-text function captioning. Frozen SaProt encoder (structure-aware vocabulary fusing residue tokens with Foldseek 3Di structural tokens) + Q-Former with 8 learnable query tokens (initialized from BiomedBERT) + frozen Galactica-1.3B decoder with LoRA. Two-stage training: stage-1 protein-text contrastive + matching + captioning objectives (different attention masks per objective); stage-2 LoRA fine-tune Galactica for captioning. Trained on 441k Swiss-Prot protein-text pairs with paired AlphaFold-DB structures. ProtBLIP2-SST-650M average 90.83 vs ProtT3-650M 89.92 vs BLIP2+ProstT5-1.5B 90.03 on 8 retrieval metrics. Field-stratified analysis: structural information helps FUNCTION descriptions most, marginal on SUBCELLULAR LOCATION and SIMILARITY (homology is sequence-level). Ablations 35M-only. Transferable BLIP-2 recipe for connecting frozen antibody LMs (AbLang, IgLM, p-IgGen) to frozen scientific LLMs without retraining either half; captioning objective is what earns alignment.

item.title: Night: ESM3 modality geometric atlas (Steenwyk, UC Berkeley, bioRxiv) — the four physical modalities fuse into a shared subspace between layers 25–35, sequence joins last after layer 28, functional-annotation stays orthogonal at every layer, universal layer-35 fusion depth across 12 organisms and 3 superkingdoms
item.description: Sunday-night single-item spotlight. Steenwyk (UC Berkeley MCB, bioRxiv 10.64898/2026.07.08.737319, posted 2026-07-12): a geometric atlas of ESM3 (esm3-sm-open-v1, 1.4B parameters, 48 transformer layers, model dim 1536) built by running the network once per modality in isolation across five input channels (sequence, structure tokens, SS8, SASA, InterPro functional annotation) plus an all-modalities reference, and reading out the residual stream at each of 48 layers. Silhouette, linear CKA, effective rank, and linear probes on 892 human proteins with replication across 5,555 proteins from 12 organisms and 177 experimentally-solved structures. Key findings: (i) the four physical modalities begin in distinct subspaces, peak separation (silhouette 0.42) at layer 24, fuse into a shared low-dim subspace by layer 35 (silhouette 0.156); (ii) fusion is ordered — structure/SS8/SASA aligned from layer 0, sequence joins last after layer 28; (iii) functional-annotation channel never fuses (pairwise CKA 0.01–0.07 vs 0.99 for physical-vs-all), and orthogonality is content-driven not granularity- or redundancy-driven (per-residue InterPro also stays orthogonal; alignment does not track whether structure recovers enzyme class); (iv) fusion is a learned property — random-weight control shows no fusion; (v) universal across the tree of life — every one of 12 organisms peaks at layer 35 exactly (std dev 0); (vi) causal leave-one-modality-out ablation: withholding function displaces the representation ~6× less than withholding structure/sequence/SASA. Direct guide to which ESM3 layer to draw embeddings from for downstream antibody-LM work and points at a clean antibody-specific follow-up experiment. Author advisory disclosure: consultant to Anthropic PBC.
item.itunes:summary: Steenwyk (UC Berkeley MCB, bioRxiv): ESM3 (esm3-sm-open-v1, 1.4B params, 48 layers) modality-in-isolation atlas across 892 human proteins (replicated on 5,555 proteins/12 organisms and 177 experimental structures). Four physical modalities (sequence, structure, SS8, SASA) begin separate, peak silhouette 0.42 at layer 24, fuse to 0.156 at layer 35; fusion is ordered with sequence joining last after layer 28. Functional-annotation channel stays orthogonal at every layer (CKA 0.01–0.07 vs 0.99 for physical fusion) regardless of granularity or redundancy with structure. Fusion is learned (random-weight control shows none) and universal — all 12 organisms peak at layer 35 exactly. Withholding function in a causal ablation displaces the representation ~6× less than withholding structure/sequence/SASA. Direct guidance for which ESM3 layer to extract embeddings from for antibody-LM fine-tuning; antibody-specific replication is a natural follow-up.

item.title: Evening: bispecific 10E8.4/iMab HIV-1 broadly neutralizing antibody phase 1 trial (David Ho lab, Nat Med) — 54 participants, safety endpoint met, delayed-rash signal in a third of PLWH; Prot-Aug — systematic ESM-2 vs ProtGPT-2 pLM-guided substitution augmentation across seven protein prediction tasks (Luo lab, HKUST, bioRxiv)
item.description: Sunday evening supplement — thin day, two items. First, Theodore/Sobieszczyk/Ho et al. item.title: Persistent single-state bias in AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and BioEmu benchmarked on four multi-state proteins (Gumbart lab, Georgia Tech); Nammu — a 167M-parameter Mamba state-space protein/metagenomic foundation model beats same-corpus transformer gLM2
item.description: Two items, Sunday morning. First, Ye, Wang, Brogi, Parks, Kuo, and Gumbart (Georgia Tech, bioRxiv): benchmark of AlphaFold3, Boltz-2, Chai-1, and BioEmu on four canonical multi-state proteins — Pf-MATE (MATE transporter, inward/outward-open), LAO (leucine-arginine-ornithine binding protein, open/closed), SecA (ATPase translocation motor), and beta-2 adrenergic receptor (class A GPCR, active/inactive); all four predictors default to the dominant PDB state; small-molecule ligands have weak and inconsistent effects on which state is emitted, but large protein partners drive clear conformational switching; MSA-based approaches (AF-Cluster and random subsampling) recapitulate similar biases, indicating the state bias is not architecture-specific and survives across diffusion/flow-based models and MSA-manipulation strategies; state bias also present in BioEmu despite explicit ensemble training. Second, Azbijari, Wynne, David, and Thurber (Oregon State, bioRxiv): Nammu, a 167M-parameter mixed-modality Mamba state-space foundation model trained on the OpenMetaGenomic (OMG) corpus with a curriculum strategy (64M protein-only sequences, then 32M mixed-modality metagenomic contigs) at 20K context length; compared against gLM2 (mixed-modality transformer on same corpus with 37 percent more tokens); Nammu outperforms gLM2 at every taxonomic level on CAMI marine dataset and on KEGG Orthology function prediction in deep-sea MAGs; linear-scaling state-space alternative to quadratic-attention transformers for long protein/nucleotide context — architectural implications for repertoire-scale antibody language modeling.

item.title: Night: AAV-encoded nanobody-IGF2 GELYAC for persistent IgG depletion (Bertozzi lab); monobody 12D4 KRAS variant selectivity computational redesign; anti-alpha-synuclein sdAb 2H1 in vivo
item.description: Saturday night supplement. Three items. First, Yang/Loh/Bertozzi et al. (Stanford, bioRxiv): genetically-encoded lysosome-targeting chimeras (GELYTACs) comprising murine IGF2 fused via 20-aa GS linker to an IgG-binding nanobody; AAV8-encoded and secreted by liver cells; bifunctional construct captures circulating IgG and routes it via IGF2R to lysosomes in receiving cells; IgG clearance demonstrated across lymphocytes, macrophages, epithelial, microglia, and hepatocytes in vitro; single AAV8 tail-vein injection sustains mGELYTAC expression for at least 77 days; IgG clearance at day 15 significantly greater than nanobody-only or non-targeting controls; mGELYTAC efficacy comparable to efgartigimod alfa at tested dose with single injection vs. weekly dosing requirement; protease-gated variant (IGFBP-masked IGF2 uncaged by granzyme B at immune synapses) and small-molecule-gated variant (X-on splicing element) enable conditional activation. Second, Kumar/Huang (Wayne State, bioRxiv): MD simulations and energy calculations on monobody 12D4 against WT KRAS and four oncogenic variants (G12C, G12D, G12V, G12R) in GTP- and GDP-bound states; conserved hydrophobic FG loop network (L77/F78/W79) anchors recognition; K75 electrostatics provide G12D selectivity; K75Q/K75Y/K75M redesigns predicted to bind G12C, G12R, and GDP-bound G12V — currently untargetable by any existing monobody; abstract-only. Third, Pragati/Congdon/Sigurdsson et al. (NYU, bioRxiv): five anti-alpha-synuclein single-domain antibodies screened in mouse neuronal culture then Drosophila synucleinopathy model; new sdAb 2H1 targeting aggregation-prone region outperforms four siblings on all disease parameters (pS129 alpha-syn clearance, DA neuron preservation, mitochondrial function, motor function, survival); turboID proximity labeling localizes interaction to synaptic/vesicle trafficking compartments; abstract-only.

item.title: Evening: antibody self-association prediction with ESM-2 plus AlphaFold residue graphs; AlphaFold 3 benchmarked for TCR antigen specificity; AbICL in-context affinity ranking; NAZ-mAb FoldX design case study
item.description: Saturday evening supplement. Four items. First, industry team (mAbs journal): antibody self-association prediction model coupling fine-tuned ESM-2 with AlphaFold-predicted residue graphs through disentangled multi-stream attention (sequence content, chain-aware positional, structural streams); CSI-BLI assay as label (246 mAbs correlates with viscosity; 41 mAbs strongly associates with Tg32 mouse clearance); 1499 IgGs and 841 VHHs, edit-distance-controlled splits; structure-aware model: VHH F1 = 0.76, IgG F1 = 0.57; sequence-only disentangled variant outperforms standard PLM baseline; complementary interpretable biophysical-descriptor model (VHH F1 = 0.72, IgG F1 = 0.57); Shapley analysis highlights charge/dipole, hydrophobicity, aggregation propensity across CDRs and framework. Second, McMaster et al. (Oxford/Rossjohn, bioRxiv): AlphaFold 3 benchmarked for TCR:pMHC antigen specificity; 100x faster MSA pipeline via TCRmodel2 databases; four model comparison (AF2/AF3/Boltz-2/Chai-1): AF3 and Chai-1 significantly outperform AF2; Boltz-2 matches AF2 only; 12 geometric/biochemical features correlated with AF3 PAE: four robust predictors (contact map, interaction count, X/Y distances over pMHC); PAE Aggregator reduces intrinsic confidence confounds; AF3 clusters sequence-similar TCRs by binding mode; mutational scanning ROCAUC 0.92/0.83 on 572G celiac antigen TCR. item.title: Afternoon: obligate trispecific IL-2R agonistic VHH antibody geometry optimization (argenx/KU Leuven, Nat Commun) for Treg-selective activation; hybrid quantum-classical GAN with photonic-quantum priors for de novo MHC class I-binding peptide design
item.description: Saturday afternoon supplement. Two items. First, Lykhopiy et al. (argenx/KU Leuven/Dualyx, Nat Commun): obligate trispecific IL-2R agonistic antibodies built from llama-derived VHHs (85 CD25 / 153 CD122 / 92 CD132 unique clones across 15/38/7 CDR3 families and 3/4/5 epitope bins), assembled by controlled Fab-arm exchange (K409R + F405L) with LALA-PG effector-silencing Fc; lead αβγVHH-48 (αVHH-2 + βVHH-19 + γVHH-27) achieves EC50 = 15 pM on HEKαβγ (vs 10 pM for human IL-2), Treg-selective activation and expansion in human PBMC, and preferential Treg expansion in humanized NSG mice at 0.03 μg dose; five bivalent-for-CD25 geometry variants (DC41/DC43/DC44/DC45/DC60) with identical specificity and valency but different spatial arrangement reveal potency-selectivity trade-off, with DC41/DC44 reaching single-digit pM-fM Treg potency and 100–1000-fold Treg-to-non-Treg window; no structural feature identified that predicts geometric outcome — target for computational antibody-format prediction. Second, Ebadi et al. (bioRxiv, HERVolution Therapeutics + ORCA Computing + Sparrow Quantum): hybrid quantum-classical pipeline coupling a GAN to latent vectors sampled from a real photonic quantum processor for de novo MHC class I-binding peptide design; tested in silico across 131 HLA alleles, quantum-derived priors increase yield of predicted strong binders with largest gains on understudied alleles; broader sequence exploration at non-anchor positions with preserved anchor specificity; wet-lab peptide-MHC stability ELISAs on three understudied alleles confirm designed peptides as potent stabilisers of pMHC class I complexes; abstract-only at time of recording.

item.title: PTIm-mAb multi-objective ML platform on 11 FDA-approved bispecifics; RFdiffusion + ProteinMPNN de novo domains reprogram plant NLR immune receptors; UMA-Inverse dense-pair ligand-conditioned inverse folding; Curr Opin Struct Biol AIR review

item.title: Evening: AbICL in-context learning for antigen-specific antibody affinity ranking; AlphaFold3 benchmarked for TCR antigen specificity with 100x speedup and PAE Aggregator

item.title: Afternoon: what protein LM pseudo-probabilities actually measure (H3N2 K lineage stress test), 1.8M-complex AlphaFold Database quaternary expansion, and Woolfson-lab all-α-helical de novo design with 75% expression rate
item.description: Afternoon addition to Friday's episode. Three items on bioRxiv. item.title: IgGM2 all-atom foundation model for immune receptor design; FlexRibbon joint sequence-structure pretraining with antibody CDR SOTA; Dayhoff Atlas 3.3B-sequence open protein LM resource
item.description: Three items today. IgGM2 (bioRxiv, Shanghai Jiao Tong University): all-atom generative framework for adaptive immune receptor design jointly generating CDR sequences and full-atom structures across antibodies, nanobodies, and T-cell receptors without fixed-backbone assumptions; structure-to-design strategy with target-conditioned structural prior; outperforms AlphaFold3 on FoldBench receptor-target geometry and improves amino-acid recovery and Rosetta interface metrics on sequence design benchmarks. FlexRibbon (bioRxiv, revised v2): 3B-parameter protein foundation model combining masked LM with diffusion-based structure denoising; hierarchical coarse-to-fine architecture; bypasses MSA dependence for mutation-rich CDR loop modeling; state-of-the-art on 12 tasks including antibody/nanobody CDR interface design; open weights. Dayhoff Atlas (bioRxiv, revised v2, Microsoft Research/Absci): GigaRef dataset of 3.34B sequences / 1.70B clusters; BackboneRef of 46M synthetic sequences from 240,811 de novo backbones; Dayhoff protein LM family combining single-sequence and MSA pretraining at scale; increased cellular expression rates of generated proteins; all data/code/models under permissive license.
item.itunes:summary: IgGM2: all-atom generative framework for antibody/nanobody/TCR CDR design + structure prediction, coupled sequence-structure generation without fixed backbone, outperforms AlphaFold3 on receptor-target geometry (FoldBench), improved AAR and Rosetta interface metrics. FlexRibbon v2: 3B protein foundation model, masked LM + diffusion denoising, hierarchical coarse-to-fine all-atom, MSA-free antibody/nanobody CDR design SOTA on 12 tasks. item.title: AstraZeneca ESM-2/AlphaFold GNN for antibody self-association developability; USP-ddG unified delta-delta-G with H1N1 CR6261 case study; A-Alpha Bio Atlas 450M affinity database launch
item.description: Three items today. First, AstraZeneca in mAbs: an ESM-2 fine-tuned protein language model fused with AlphaFold residue graphs via disentangled multi-stream attention predicts CSI-BLI self-association class across 1,499 IgGs and 841 VHHs with edit-distance-controlled splits; structure-aware model achieves F1 = 0.76 for VHH and 0.57 for IgG; Shapley analysis highlights CDR charge/dipole and hydrophobicity as dominant drivers. item.title: Evening: convergent HCDR-2 improbable mutations drive V3-glycan bnAb maturation across primates, and tandem scFv-Fc bispecific IL-7 receptor agonist engineering
item.description: Evening addition to today's episodes. First, a Science Translational Medicine paper from the Williams/Haynes groups at Duke (with Korber at Los Alamos and Shaw at Penn): 18 SHIV BG505-infected rhesus macaques recapitulate convergent HIV envelope evolution, and three develop V3-glycan broadly neutralizing antibodies. From the highest-breadth macaque, 203 members of a clonal lineage (DH1030) are isolated; DH1030 shares striking genetic, functional, and structural similarity with the human V3-glycan bnAb DH270 — most notably a glycine-to-arginine improbable mutation at HCDR2 position 56 (macaque) or 57 (human) that makes direct contact with the GDIR V3 motif and is required for heterologous neutralization in both lineages. PheBAR-seq single-cell BCR and transcriptome profiling of lymph node and spleen shows this improbable mutation is the trigger for GC exit into memory; a compensatory S114P HCDR3 mutation follows. V1-glycan-deleted Env variants prime both lineages, directly informing ongoing clinical trials of BG505-based immunogens. Second, from the Yea group at DGIST in Korea (PEDS, abstract-only): TB4, a tetravalent tandem scFv-Fc bispecific antibody, cis-engages IL-7 receptor alpha and the common gamma chain, outperforming the knobs-into-holes format in affinity and avidity, reduces receptor internalization, sustains STAT5 phosphorylation, and selectively expands CD4+ effector memory T cells with a distinct antiviral transcriptomic signature.
item.itunes:summary: Williams/Haynes/Korber/Shaw (Science Translational Medicine): 18 SHIV BG505-infected rhesus macaques recapitulate convergent HIV Env evolution; three develop V3-glycan bnAbs; DH1030 (203-member macaque lineage) shares an improbable HCDR2 Gly-to-Arg mutation at the same structural position as human DH270 — both mutations contact the GDIR V3 motif and are required for heterologous neutralization breadth. PheBAR-seq shows the improbable mutation drives GC exit to memory; V1-glycan-deleted Envs prime both human and macaque lineages. Yea/DGIST (PEDS): TB4 tetravalent tandem scFv-Fc bispecific cis-engages IL-7Ra and gc, outperforms knobs-into-holes format, reduces receptor internalization, sustains STAT5, selectively expands CD4+ effector memory T cells with antiviral transcriptomic signature.

item.title: Afternoon: a Nussenzweig-lab biophysical model for what IgD does — hinge entropy sets B-cell selection thresholds — and a 22-model zero-shot benchmark of protein language models on a real thermostability landscape from Jewett, Marks, and Notin
item.description: Afternoon add-on to today's morning episode. First, a Nussenzweig-lab preprint (with theory from Chakraborty at MIT and single-molecule from Blanchard) offers a physical answer to the sixty-year-old question of what IgD is for: single-molecule measurements show the antigen-binding arms of IgD are substantially more dynamic than IgM's, imposing an entropic cost on bivalent antigen capture. Mouse genetics — IgM-only, IgD-only, IgM+IgD, and hinge-truncated-IgD lines — confirm that the entropic penalty attenuates negative selection by self-antigen and raises the affinity threshold for positive selection into the germinal center. The B-cell-receptor hinge dynamics themselves are a tunable parameter of the selection landscape, with direct implications for repertoire modeling and affinity maturation. Second, a Jewett/Marks/Notin/Beckham preprint benchmarks 22 zero-shot protein fitness models on a real thermostability landscape: cell-free expression coupled to a gas-phase CO2 colorimetric assay produces a saturation scan of a thermostable carbonic anhydrase — 4,365 single-AA mutations across 39,285 reactions at 70C and 90C — then closes the loop by filtering a 100,000-variant ProteinMPNN library with zero-shot PLMs plus supervised heads down to 419 characterized variants, producing a best-in-class enzyme still active after 95C incubation. Directly translatable methodology for antibody developability.
item.itunes:summary: Nussenzweig-lab preprint: single-molecule dynamics show IgD antigen-binding arms are more mobile than IgM's, imposing an entropic penalty on bivalent antigen capture; mouse genetics with tailored isotype configurations (IgM-only, IgD-only, hinge-truncated IgD) show the penalty attenuates negative selection by self-antigen and raises the affinity threshold for germinal-center entry — BCR hinge dynamics are a tunable selection parameter. Jewett/Marks/Notin/Beckham: cell-free expression plus gas-phase CO2 assay maps a full single-AA saturation landscape of a thermostable carbonic anhydrase (4,365 mutations, 39,285 reactions, 70C and 90C), benchmarks 22 zero-shot protein fitness models on it, then filters a 100,000-variant ProteinMPNN library down to 419 characterized variants; best variant active after 95C incubation.

item.title: AbICL in-context learning for antibody affinity ranking, and IgG agalactosylation is anti-inflammatory not pro-inflammatory
item.description: Two items today. AbICL (arXiv) introduces in-context learning for antigen-specific antibody affinity ranking: a structural encoder paired with a context ranking head, trained with episodic meta-learning so the model can use a small support set of labeled comparisons from the same campaign at inference time without gradient updates. Outperforms ranking baselines on AbRank, with the largest gains under distribution shift and fine-grained discrimination. Second, a bioRxiv preprint from the Vermeren lab at Edinburgh challenges the dogma that agalactosylated IgG is pro-inflammatory: engineered agalactosylated immune complexes generate less neutrophil reactive oxygen species than galactosylated complexes, due to weaker Fc-gamma-receptor binding and lower AKT/p38 MAPK activation. The result suggests agalactosylation may be a compensatory anti-inflammatory mechanism rather than a driver of pathology, with direct implications for glycan engineering.
item.itunes:summary: AbICL: in-context learning for antibody affinity ranking using episodic meta-training; a structural encoder and context ranking head that uses support-set labeled comparisons at test time without fine-tuning; best gains on AbRank under distribution shift and fine-grained ranking. IgG N-glycan agalactosylation: Vermeren lab shows agalactosylated IgG immune complexes reduce neutrophil ROS production vs. galactosylated — weaker FcgammaR binding, lower AKT/p38 activation — suggesting the disease-associated glycoform is anti-inflammatory rather than pro-inflammatory.

item.title: Evening: FCRL5 as a fucose-sensitive IgG Fc receptor with an E293R selective-knockout mutation, ThermoFusion's OOD case for structure-plus-sequence delta-delta-G, and Woolfson-lab de novo bifunctional PROTACs
item.description: Fourth pass through the July seventh bio-archive drop. First, the Rispens group at Sanquin nails down the FCRL5-IgG interaction: 60-80 microMolar affinity driven by the two N-terminal FCRL5 domains with essential Fc-tail residues distinct from classical Fc-gamma receptors, considerable preference for afucosylated IgG, and — the engineering payload — E293R as a single-residue Fc mutation that selectively abrogates FCRL5 binding while preserving every classical Fc-gamma receptor. A clean companion to the morning's CD16a story. Second, ThermoFusion (Novartis, Basel) fuses ThermoMPNN 3D-structure embeddings with ESM-2 sequence embeddings for delta-delta-G prediction, holds up on out-of-distribution enzyme sequences where ThermoMPNN alone and state-of-the-art tools collapse, and stands in direct tension with the bonus round's sequence-only ESM-2 delta-Tm claim. Third, the Woolfson lab at Bristol builds a full de-novo protein-based PROTAC: a 67-residue helix-loop-helix scaffold (sc-apCC-2), a 3 nanoMolar BCL-xL binder from hot-spot grafting plus ProteinMPNN with a shape-complementarity negative-selection step yielding >1000x selectivity against MCL-1, a KLHL20 SLiM in the loop, and endogenous BCL-xL degradation in A549 cells on par with the clinical PROTAC DT2216. FCRL5 read from abstract-plus-body; ThermoFusion abstract-only (body not yet rendered); TPD paper read in full.

ThermoFusion (Novartis) fuses ThermoMPNN structure embeddings with ESM-2 for delta-delta-G, holds up out-of-distribution where prior tools collapse, and pushes back on the bonus round's sequence-only claim. item.title: Late add: PGLD from Reddy and Krause at ETH — policy-gradient library design bridging generative sequence models and high-throughput screens, demonstrated on a broadly neutralizing influenza antibody
item.description: A short late-afternoon add-on. A bio-archive preprint posted this morning from Scott Sussex, Sai Reddy, and Andreas Krause at E-T-H Zurich introduces PGLD — Policy Gradients for Library Design — which parametrizes stochastic DNA libraries in a synthesis-aware way and optimizes the library's distribution against a specified objective. The framing bridges two poles that have dominated in-silico antibody design: deterministic per-sequence synthesis (controlled but capped by cost) and blind degenerate libraries (cheap but wasteful). PGLD closes the loop for lab-in-the-loop multi-round experiments and lets generative models be sampled at wet-lab scale. The headline demonstration: a library of roughly ten to the sixth unique sequences, synthesized for about seven hundred U-S dollars, to explore the mutation space of a broadly neutralizing influenza antibody. Take is drawn from the abstract only — the body has not yet rendered — and open questions on objective, screening readout, and paired-chain handling are noted in the segment.
item.itunes:summary: PGLD (Sussex, Reddy, Krause, E-T-H Zurich) parametrizes stochastic DNA libraries in a synthesis-aware way and optimizes them against an objective function using policy gradients, bridging generative sequence models and high-throughput screens. Enables closed-loop multi-round design and large-scale in-vitro sampling from generative models. Demonstrated on a ~10^6-sequence library synthesized at ~$700 to explore the mutation space of a broadly neutralizing influenza antibody. Segment drawn from the abstract only — body not yet rendered.

item.title: Bonus round: an AlphaFold benchmark on antibody and TCR complexes, sequence-only ESM2 for melting-temperature prediction, and a synthetic-sdAb linkage-specific ubiquitin binder
item.description: Bonus segment for July seventh. Three more items from the July sixth biorxiv drop. A Pierce-lab benchmark from U-Maryland IBBR of AlphaFold2, AlphaFold3, and increased sampling protocols across antibody-protein, antibody-peptide, and TCR-pMHC complex modeling: AF3 and sampling both help, antibody-peptide is the hardest interface class despite small antigen size, and per-case complementarity lets a model-pooling strategy lift antibody-peptide near-native success from 41% to 59%. A Genedata sequence-only paper argues that a carefully tuned ESM2-650M model beats structure-informed baselines for delta-Tm prediction — the interesting content is the ablation of loss, pooling, auxiliary supervision, and fine-tuning regime — and it stands in productive tension with the ESM+MM/GBSA benchmark from this morning's episode. And a Damgaard-lab paper reports 2A6, a synthetic-human single-domain antibody with nanomolar affinity and strict specificity for M1-linked polyubiquitin chains — the first sdAb targeting a homotypic linkage — with the AlphaFold3-predicted binding mode corroborated by saturation mutagenesis and validated across ELISA, IB, IP, and IF.
item.itunes:summary: Bonus segment for July seventh. Pierce-lab benchmark: AF3 + sampling help, antibody-peptide is the hardest class, and pooling lifts near-native success from 41% to 59%. Genedata argues a well-tuned ESM2-650M beats structure-informed methods for delta-Tm — in productive tension with today's morning ESM+MM/GBSA episode.
